title: Execution targets and rebind
summary: Frozen targets and digests stay as provenance across authorized takeover and never gate a write. Current execution ownership, same-target ancestry, tenant/project/member or shared-group authority and endpoint checks remain required. QA tests whatever is deployed: QA start reports a different served commit and proceeds, and every deployment-bound browser case records the commit its environment served at case start. Once the successor has a ready deploy receipt, execution and mission views name its pinned release_version, and command cases check out the current owning run's project source. A takeover tells each moved member owner once that QA moved to the successor and opens at its item QA stage; the predecessor wake is not the command. An owner whose carried walk is still open under a live session gets no takeover notice and no successor stage wake: the walk keeps going and may pass on the newer build. An inherited fail whose latest failing attempt was created before this run, and whose merge is in the current release, retries with yoke qa plan run --item REF --stage STAGE --project SLUG. A failure created after this run gets the ordinary rework handoff. Materialization rebinds open private and run QA requirements in place to the successor receipt, keeping each case ID and prior target JSON. A predecessor pass carries only across the same destination, including repeated takeovers; otherwise the case is owed again. An open shared plan group keeps its group identity, pinned cases and case IDs, and once its owning run holds a newer ready receipt (after takeover or a redeploy) dispatch or the next group run rebinds every live group case to that target, carrying same-destination passes; a group whose walk has begun keeps its target. Begun executions and captures keep their frozen targets, and a walk whose requirement was rebound keeps running host commands and walk-end against its frozen case while a changed definition, position or starting run still refuses; an execution that has run, leased and recorded nothing, such as one waiting for its Test Machine turn, takes the successor's current roster and target when its owner begins it again or the host-turn wake resumes it by execution id, keeping its execution ID, execution_order and host-line place, for member executions and plan-group walks alike. Neither observation changes nor early verdicts grant release approval. Manual-only takeover notices tell holders without a future scheduled wake to check the evidence and schedule their next recheck before parking; no dispatch wakes them for it. Steering recipients must staff the item for that check. Holders with future scheduled rechecks receive no manual-only takeover notice; automatic or mixed requirements keep successor dispatch guidance.
